# fuzz sweep: hundreds of runs, one line per seed, no per-step text.
# Generated by tools/gen_fuzz_fixture.py --sweep; do not edit.
# Reproduce a line by running tests/fuzz_sweep.rs, or dump one seed with
#     python tools/gen_fuzz_fixture.py --detail <SEED>
# which writes fixtures/fuzz_<SEED>.txt for tests/fuzz_fixture.rs.
#
# Every blind's target is forced to 1 chip before each step, and the action
# is chosen by the game's own RunRng (rng.rs): seed
#     "fuzz-sweep:<seed>:<deck>:<stake>"  pool "choose".
# The sweep carries no action sequence, so both engines must reproduce that
# chooser -- which rng.rs already does bit for bit. The committed detail
# seeds keep Python's random.Random; their sequence is emitted verbatim.
#
# FNV-1a-64 rolls over the concatenation of every step's canonical bytes,
# the rendering tools/state_render.py gives for a tree of
#     {action, legal_order, legal_sorted, rng, state}
# (the same leaves the detailed `digests`/`legal` columns hash). FNV-1a is
# incremental, so folding one step at a time equals hashing the run at once.
#
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   seed deck stake steps over capped deepest final checkpoints
#     over        1 if the run ended by itself
#     capped      1 if it hit its step cap instead
#     deepest     deepest ante any recorded step saw (always < 16)
#     final       one-shot digest of the post-run state_dict leaves
#     checkpoints `step=<16 hex>` at every 25 steps, plus the final step,
#   so a mismatch localises to one 25-step block, not the whole run.
#
# Runs stay under ante 16: `ante_base_chips` saturates i64 from 16 up while
# Python's int does not, so the `blinds` row diverges there by design.
